title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds an autotune job that recommends batching and caching defaults, new quantization profile configs, and a unit-economics report generator for route-level cost estimates. Non-breaking by default; opt-in via project config.
description:
Context: This PR implements the first iteration of automated cost-optimization tooling: an autotune service that recommends batching and KV-caching defaults per route, quantization profile registration and sample profiles for common open models, and a developer-facing unit-economics report tied to routes and workload traces.
Motivation: shipping clear, automated recommendations reduces manual tuning and helps customers lower per-token cost while preserving output quality (ENG-2214, ENG-2241, PM-342).
Scope:
- Autotune worker that analyzes recent traces and suggests batch_size, max_latency_target, and cache_prefix_expiry defaults.
- Schema and registration for quantization profiles (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) with heuristics based on model architecture and latency budget.
- Unit-economics report generator that calculates cost-per-1K-tokens, estimated savings from caching/batching/quantization, and shows confidence bands.
- Console hooks: a new route-level recommendations panel and downloadable CSV report.
- API: /autotune/v1/recommendations (read-only) and /uecon/v1/reports/{route} (auth required).
Commits summary:
1) Add autotune worker, analysis pipeline, and a lightweight scheduler (3 commits)
2) Add quant profile schema, sample profiles, and model heuristics (2 commits)
3) Unit-econ report generator and CSV export (2 commits)
4) Console integration and UI endpoint (2 commits)
5) Tests, e2e scenario, and perf tuning (3 commits)
Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/autotune/: new worker, trace ingestion, and heuristic engine.
- runtime/quant_profiles/: schema, registry, and sample profiles.
- console/frontend/src/routes/: recommendations panel and report download.
- console/backend/api/: new endpoints and auth checks.
- infra/cron/: scheduled job spec for autotune.
- tests/autotune_integration_test.py and tests/uecon_report_test.py (new).
Notable code snippets (illustrative):
- autotune heuristic: "if median_latency > target && p95_tokens > 8: recommend batch_size = min(64, p95_tokens)"
- quant registration example: "quant_profile: q4_1; recommended_for: ['llama-2-13b', 'gptj-6b']"
Review conversation (summary):
- Priya: "Can we make recommendations opt-out per-project?" Author: "Yes — added project_config.autotune.enabled with default true; doc note added."
- Ethan: "Needs safety guard: do not recommend bizarro batch sizes for interactive routes." Author: "Added route-type-aware bounds and a tests matrix."
- Liam: "Unit econ calculation should surface currency and region assumptions." Author: "Included region tag and compute cost assumptions in CSV export; added note to console."
- QA (Riley): "Saw intermittent e2e failure on sample trace upload." Author: "Root cause: test fixture race; added retry and idempotent trace ingestion."
CI and testing:
- Local unit tests: pass.
- CI: initial run had failing e2e due to test race; after fix CI passed on rerun.
- Performance: autotune worker CPU usage within budget; sample runs show recommended configs reduce estimated per-token cost by 12-28% depending on workload profile.
Security & privacy:
- Trace ingestion strips user identifiers and samples traces by route only.
- API endpoints require existing service scope; console UI respects RBAC.
Migration/ops notes:
- Autotune scheduler initially disabled in release config; rollout via feature flag enabled for white-listed customers.
- Quant profiles are additive; registering new profiles won't change serving defaults until explicitly applied.
Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (this PR).
2) Internal dogfood: enable for dev/staging routes for 2 weeks.
3) Gradual enable on small set of customers and gather feedback.
4) Public rollout with documentation and console tour.
Linear/Jira links: ENG-2214 (autotune core), ENG-2241 (quant profile registry), PM-342 (unit econ design).
Merge: squash and merge, commit message includes a short changelog and references to Linear.
Notes:
- Tests added for route-type bounds and for quant profile selection.
- Docs entry in console docs will be added in a follow-up small PR by docs team.
- Performance numbers are derived from a 48-hour trace sample of production-like dev workloads.
